rationale: The plant uses a hazardous chemical, so it must maintain a written hazard communication program, have an SDS in the workplace, and ensure workplace containers are labeled, tagged, or marked. Introduction of a new chemical hazard on which employees have not previously been trained requires effective information and training at introduction. The training must cover detection methods, chemical hazards, protective measures, and the employer's hazard communication program, labels, and SDSs. The portable-container immediate-use exception is not applied because the supplied facts do not establish that transferred containers are intended only for the immediate use of the employee performing the transfer.

Because the technician is the employer's employee and is newly assigned to work in the covered process area, the employer must provide effective hazardous-chemical information and training at the time of the initial assignment. The training must address the listed hazard detection methods, chemical hazards, protective measures, and hazard communication program/SDS and labeling information.

Federal OSHA PSM applies, and the significant equipment and technology modification is expressly not a replacement in kind. The employer must use written management-of-change procedures, update affected process safety information, and review operating procedures as necessary to reflect the changed technology and equipment. Before highly hazardous chemicals are introduced and production is restarted, the pre-startup safety review must confirm conformity with design specifications, adequate safety/operating/maintenance/emergency procedures, completion of management of change for the modified facility, and completed training for each employee operating the process. Because hazardous chemicals are being introduced, employees must receive effective hazard communication training when a new chemical hazard not previously covered in their training is introduced, including the required hazard, protective-measure, emergency-procedure, labeling, and SDS information.

Federal OSHA PSM applies, and the near miss at the covered process could reasonably have resulted in a catastrophic toxic release. Therefore, the employer must investigate the incident under §1910.119(m)(1). The absence of an employee injury does not negate this investigation trigger. The supplied facts do not establish an OSHA fatality, hospitalization, amputation, loss-of-eye, or recordable-injury reporting trigger.

Because the recordkeeping-covered establishment had 300 employees during the calendar year covered by the annual summary, it must create and certify the OSHA 300A annual summary, post it conspicuously without alteration or obstruction no later than February 1 through April 30, electronically submit OSHA Form 300A information to OSHA or its designee, and retain the OSHA 300 Log, any privacy case list, annual summary, and OSHA 301 forms for five years after the covered calendar year.

The described equipment servicing falls within the supplied lockout/tagout context because unexpected energization or stored energy could cause injury. As the anniversary of the last machine-specific energy-control procedure review approaches, the employer must conduct the periodic inspection at least annually to ensure that the procedure and the standard's requirements are being followed.

The scenario is covered servicing under the hazardous-energy-control standard and identifies hazards from unexpected startup and stored pneumatic energy. The employer must maintain an energy-control program; develop, document, and use energy-control procedures; train employees; isolate the machine from its energy source through energy-isolating devices; and relieve, disconnect, restrain, or otherwise render stored pneumatic energy safe after lockout/tagout devices are applied.

Because the contractor is being selected to perform work in a covered PSM process area, the host employer must obtain and evaluate the contract employer's safety-performance and program information before selection. The host employer must inform the contract employer of known potential fire, explosion, and toxic-release hazards and must implement safe work practices controlling contractor entrance, presence, and exit. The contract employer must assure each contract employee is instructed on known job- and process-related hazards and applicable emergency-action-plan provisions. The host employer also must maintain the contract-employee injury and illness log related to contractor work in process areas.

The requester is a former employee seeking the OSHA 301 Incident Report describing that former employee's own injury. The employer maintains the report and is covered by federal OSHA recordkeeping rules. The employer must provide a copy containing that information by the end of the next business day.

Because an authorized employee representative has made a valid request for OSHA 301 Incident Reports concerning represented employees at the establishment, the employer must provide copies within 7 calendar days. The copies may include only the OSHA 301 section titled "Tell us about the case"; all other information must be removed.

The establishment is recordkeeping-covered, and the case is stated to be work-related and new. Death satisfies the general recording criteria; therefore, the fatality must be recorded. The death also triggers a report to OSHA within eight hours after the death resulting from the work-related incident.

The work-related incident resulted in both an employee amputation and in-patient hospitalization. The employer must report the event to OSHA within 24 hours. Because the case is stated to be recordable and the employer learned of it today, it must be entered on the OSHA 300 Log and 301 Incident Report within seven calendar days of receiving that information.

The new-employee orientation supports application of the duty to inform each employee of the injury-and-illness reporting procedure. The supervisor's threatened discipline following a report of a work-related injury is conduct covered by the prohibition on discharging or otherwise discriminating against an employee for reporting. It also indicates that the reporting procedure must be assessed for whether it would deter or discourage a reasonable employee from accurate reporting. No supplied facts establish that the injury is recordable or triggers a fatality, hospitalization, amputation, or eye-loss report.

Because the covered process is undergoing its required three-year PSM compliance audit and deficiencies were identified, the employer must certify the triennial compliance evaluation, promptly determine and document an appropriate response to every audit finding, document correction of deficiencies, and retain the two most recent compliance-audit reports.

The vessel is process equipment in a covered PSM process, and the scheduled inspection found it outside acceptable limits. The employer must correct the deficiency before further use, or in a safe and timely manner when necessary means are taken to assure safe operation. Selecting between these compliance paths requires qualified safety or engineering judgment about whether continued operation can be safely assured and what corrective action and timing are appropriate.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: The record does not state whether necessary means are available and implemented to assure safe operation pending correction, nor does it provide the engineering basis needed to determine whether the vessel may remain in use or must be removed from service before further use.

rationale: The employee handles a hazardous chemical used by the employer in the employee's work area. The employer must have an SDS for that chemical in the workplace and must ensure that it is readily accessible during every work shift when employees are in their work areas. The stated inability to immediately access the SDS during the night shift indicates the immediate-access condition is not met.

The portable container is filled from a labeled drum, is intended only for the immediate use of the employee performing the transfer, remains under that employee's control, and is not stored for later use. Therefore, the stated portable-container labeling exception applies and the employer is not required to label this portable container.

The supplied OSHA excerpt establishes the default rule: each lockout or tagout device must be removed by the employee who applied it. Because management proposes removal by another employee, the supplied context does not establish that the proposed action is authorized or compliant. Determining whether any permissible exception procedure applies requires safety and procedural judgment not supplied in the excerpts.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Escalate to qualified safety management. Needed information includes whether the employer has an established, authorized procedure governing removal of a device when the applying employee is unavailable, and whether its required safeguards and verification steps can be met. The supplied excerpt states only the default removal rule and does not supply an exception process.

rationale: Because one employer produces, uses, or stores hazardous chemicals in a manner that may expose another on-site employer's workers, the employer must ensure its written hazard communication program specifies the method for providing the other employer on-site access to the safety data sheet for each hazardous chemical.

The reactor component swap is an equipment change in a PSM-covered process. Section 1910.119(l)(1) requires written management-of-change procedures unless the work is a replacement in kind. The documented different material specification and operating limit, together with the engineering/operations disagreement, prevent a determinate replacement-in-kind conclusion and require qualified engineering and safety review.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Resolve whether the proposed component is technically equivalent to the existing design and operating basis, including compatibility of the changed material specification and operating limit with the process safety information and applicable design specifications. The supplied facts present a technical conflict requiring qualified engineering and safety judgment.

rationale: A report within 24 hours is required only when an employee's in-patient hospitalization results from a work-related incident. The supplied facts establish an illness and hospital admission but do not establish either required predicate.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the illness resulted from a work-related incident and whether the hospital admission was an in-patient hospitalization.

rationale: New-product procurement can trigger hazard-communication training when a new chemical hazard, not previously covered by employee training, is introduced into the work area. The supplied facts do not establish either condition.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine from the product safety data sheet whether the cleaning product is hazardous, and determine whether its hazards are new to the affected employees' prior hazard-communication training.

rationale: The vendor is outside servicing personnel, but the coordination requirement applies only when the vendor is engaged in activities covered by the scope and application of the lockout/tagout standard. The supplied facts do not establish whether the maintenance involves a machine or equipment for which unexpected energization, startup, or release of stored energy could occur and cause injury. If that predicate is met, the on-site and outside employers must inform each other of their respective lockout or tagout procedures.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the planned maintenance could expose personnel to injury from unexpected energization, startup, or stored-energy release. If so, the work is within the described LOTO scope and outside-employer coordination is required.

rationale: Electronic submission of OSHA Form 300A information applies to an establishment that had 20-249 employees at any time during the previous calendar year and is classified in an industry listed in Appendix A. The stated 75-employee count does not establish the required industry classification, and it is not expressly tied to the previous-calendar-year period.
missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Provide the establishment's industry classification and confirm whether it had 20-249 employees at any time during the previous calendar year.
